scope: Proposition 5.1 (General realization) of the manuscript “Variable-dimension Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence on general and subcubic graphs” (preprints/Variable-dimension-Weisfeiler-Leman-equivalence-on-general-and-subcubic-graphs-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 133 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5b3048ce062b1b8e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the affine block data at address length r ≥ 3, the graphs G0, G1 are simple, uncolored, and of the same positive order. They have O(J3) vertices. Every ξB ∈ Z1 B determines a fixed bijection ΨB,ξB : V 0 B → V 1 B, depending only on B, ξB, by (B, z) |−→ (B, z + ξB), leaf(B, z, ν) |−→ leaf(B, z + ξB, ν). For any set U of blocks, offsets agreeing on all shared readouts make the union of these maps an isomorphism of the induced subgraphs on the corresponding parts. At every history reached by a winning K = r + 1-slot strategy, a marked base vertex (B, z) is answered by (B, z′) with z′ ∈ Z1 B. If zero base vertices of distinct blocks are simultaneously marked, their responses agree on every shared readout, even when all K slots are occupied.
